LITTLE RITUALS. LESS WASTE.
START WITH WHAT'S THERE

Your fridge has
plans for dinner.

A receipt. A handwritten list. That half-full crisper. Bring the food you've already bought into the plan, then give it a useful next step.

Text recognition runs on your device. You review the matches. Fridge photos can be added as a visual reference and labelled by you.

How this works · assumptions, privacy & sources

This is an interactive, deterministic simulator. The starting kitchen is sample inventory. Days are a relative Monday–Sunday planning week. Quantities use one adult portion and 0.6 per child. Whole packs round up; weight quantities round to 0.1 kg. Your existing food is allocated to meals before its planning date, and remaining ingredients go into the nearest planned shop. The simulator's inventory projection subtracts planned meals before the selected day; it does not confirm that anything was cooked or purchased.

Simulator prices, planning dates and store profiles are editable assumptions. The separate shopping companions read selected product prices from the customer’s shopping page. Those snapshots do not replace these simulation assumptions. There are no verified savings, special-offer predictions or guaranteed best shopping days. Shop comparisons include the trip costs you enter. Frozen food needs a safe thawing and cooking plan. Check packaging and MPI guidance.

Settings are saved in this browser, without retailer passwords. Uploaded images remain in memory and are discarded on reload; receipt text is processed locally with Tesseract.js. Text matching covers the foods in this planner. There is no food-photo recognition. Each optional browser companion uses the customer’s own retailer session and stores its shopping records in browser-session memory. It never reads passwords or payment fields. Every trolley addition requires approval in the companion; checkout remains with the retailer. Both pilots still need signed-in end-to-end validation. Woolworths currently supports one fixed-price pack per approval and pickup stores; weighed foods and larger quantities are adjusted directly on Woolworths.

Food images: Unsplash. Kitchen film: Pressmaster / Pexels. 3D kitchen made for assembl using Three.js.

 VISION LIST · REVIEW BEFORE ADDING

See it. List it. Use it.

Choose a receipt or written list for text recognition. For a fridge photo, keep it beside you and select the foods you can see.

Matches start at 1 unit each with editable dates. Correct quantities in your kitchen. Text recognition can make mistakes and cannot identify food safety.

Set up the desktop pilot

This version needs the companion in desktop Chrome. It is a locally installed pilot, not yet a Chrome Web Store release. It does not work inside the Codex in-app browser or on mobile.

  1. Download and extract the companion.
  2. In Chrome, open chrome://extensions, enable Developer mode and choose Load unpacked. Select the extracted companion folder.
  3. Open the extension and choose Enable browser connection. Approve access to this Kitchen Machine site and New World.
  4. Open Kitchen Machine in the same Chrome profile, check the connection, then send one shop. Sign in directly on New World.
Download companion ↓Read pilot scope & setup ↗

Independent assembl pilot. No New World or Foodstuffs partnership is claimed. A signed-in customer test is still required before broader use. Product prices may change; final weight, promotions and service fees are confirmed by New World.
